settings.bandwidthStale: Set to {kbps} kbit/s, but Windows has restarted since: apply it again.
settings.bandwidthHint: Caps outbound (upload) traffic only, for all Roblox clients together, as a Windows QoS policy. Applying needs admin rights (Windows asks each time) and lasts until Windows restarts.
settings.shutdownHintClose: Windows' own shutdown timer. When it runs out, Windows closes every app without asking, so unsaved work elsewhere is lost. MTwin Manager's clients are closed 30 s before (if MTwin Manager hasn't restarted since). Cancel it here, even after a restart of MTwin Manager.
settings.shutdownHint: Windows' own shutdown timer. When it runs out, Windows closes every app without asking, so unsaved work elsewhere is lost. Cancel it here, even after a restart of MTwin Manager.
settings.publicHint: Turned off, MTwin Manager doesn't launch on a network Windows calls Public (café, hotel, school Wi-Fi), and a master-password vault locks there.
settings.publicConfirmText: Others on a public network can see which servers your clients connect to, and can try to reach this PC. With this on, MTwin Manager launches there too. Only turn it on for a network you trust, and turn it off again after.
settings.upToDate: MTwin Manager is up to date.
settings.backgroundCovers: The theme covers {n}% of the picture
settings.encryptionHintMaster: Asked at start and after auto-lock.
settings.encryptionHintDpapi: Windows DPAPI: unlocks with your Windows sign-in, no prompt.
settings.antiAfkHowHint: Only after 5 s without keyboard or mouse input: each client is brought to the front for a moment (a minimized one is restored, then minimized again), gets an F13 press (no game uses it, so the character stays put) and the window you had in front comes back. Roblox only counts a real key press in the window in front.
settings.publicNotNow: Not on a public network now.
settings.importWrongPassword: Wrong password, or the file is damaged.
settings.robloxMissing: Roblox isn't installed. Install it here or from roblox.com.
settings.openLogsHint: MTwin Manager's own logs, for a bug report
settings.languageHint: Windows follows the Windows display language when MTwin Manager has it, else English.
settings.densityHint: Row height in the accounts list.
settings.discordHint: Your Discord profile shows “Playing MTwin Manager” with the game and how many alts run. Only while Discord is open on this PC.
settings.closeToTrayHint: The window hides; running clients and auto-rejoin keep working.
settings.skipSplashHint: Opens MTwin Manager right away, without the start-up animation. Applies from the next start.
settings.liteUiHint: For laptops and older PCs: no animations, blur or shadows, live pictures once a second, and the window drawn without the graphics card from the next start.
settings.multiHint: MTwin Manager holds Roblox's single-instance lock while it runs, so each account gets its own client. Turn it on before the first client starts.
settings.protectLoginHint: While MTwin Manager's clients run, lock Roblox's shared sign-in files so clients can't overwrite each other's session (error 773, wrong account in game). Meanwhile Roblox's own app can't save its sign-in.
settings.launchDelayHint: Wait between two launches when several accounts launch at once. About a second either way is added.
settings.minimizeHint: Each client is minimized once, when it first reaches a game, without taking the focus; full-quality accounts stay visible. Home shows its last picture. Anti-AFK in focus mode skips minimized clients, so use In the background.
settings.autoRejoinHint: Relaunch a client Roblox disconnects (kicked, server shut down, connection lost) into the same target.
settings.autoRestartHint: Relaunch a client that closes without MTwin Manager closing it, or whose window stops responding for 30 s. Closing Roblox's window yourself looks the same, so close clients from MTwin Manager.
settings.antiAfkHint: So Roblox doesn't disconnect idle clients after 20 minutes, each client in a game gets a key press. A client can opt out under its limits on Home.
settings.antiAfkEveryHint: Roblox disconnects after 20 idle minutes, so 1 to 19.
settings.breakerHint: Rejoins and restarts of one account within this time. Each waits twice as long as the one before (at most a minute); past the limit MTwin Manager leaves it and tells you.
settings.closeGraceHint: How long a client MTwin Manager closes gets to close by itself before it is ended.
settings.launchArgsHint: Extra words for every client, after its launch link (for a bootstrapper, say). No quotes or & | < > ^. An account can have its own in its details.
settings.fpsCapHint: The frame rate each client MTwin Manager starts is capped at, unless the account has its own. MTwin Manager sets Roblox's own Maximum Frame Rate just before the client starts and puts yours back once the client has read it; a batch does so for each launch. Off leaves Roblox alone.
settings.lowGraphicsHint: Clients MTwin Manager starts use Roblox's lowest graphics quality, which saves a lot of GPU and CPU with many clients. Your own Roblox graphics setting is put back right after, and again when such a client closes (or, if MTwin Manager isn't running then, when it next starts).
settings.autoUpdateHint: When Roblox has a new version and no Roblox client runs (nor a launch or batch), install it. The installer is checked to be signed by Roblox Corporation first. Never over a bootstrapper such as Bloxstrap, which updates Roblox itself.
settings.memRestartHint: Close and relaunch a client whose commit size stays over this for 30 s, into the same game, within the restart limit in Settings, Launching. Not during a batch. It disconnects the client, but it's the only way to free its private memory.
settings.memThrottleHint: While a client's commit size is over this, hold it to the CPU limit below, which lowers its frame rate. Lifted once it is back under 90 %. Tightens a client's own limit, never loosens it.
settings.trimHint: Ask Windows to page each client's memory out on a schedule, and sooner if it grows; it comes back as used. A client's own limit on Home wins.
settings.spreadHint: Give each client its own share of the cores, round-robin. Cores picked for a client on Home win. Skipped when there are too few cores for two per client.
settings.adaptiveHint: Clients whose window isn't in front get the limits below; the one you're playing runs free. A limit set on one client wins over these.
settings.adaptiveBgHint: CPU limit (a share of all cores), efficiency mode and how often to trim memory, for clients not in front.
settings.fairCapHint: Divides the CPU among the clients, so each gets a smaller cap as more run. The client in front, clients loading or not responding and Full quality accounts run free. A client's own limit on Home wins.
settings.panicHint: Works from any app, even a game in front: stops every Roblox client at once, like the Hold to stop all button. Modifiers and one key, like Ctrl+Shift+F12. Empty turns it off.
settings.cleanLogsHint: Delete Roblox's client logs over a day old or over 50 MB, at start and every hour. A running client's log is kept.
settings.masterPasswordHint: Changing it only re-wraps the key; cookies are not re-encrypted.
settings.autoLockHint: Locks the vault and wipes the key from memory.
settings.clipboard: Clear clipboard after copying a cookie
settings.cacheHint: How long the info panel reuses what Roblox said before asking again. Presence refreshes every minute while Accounts is open.
settings.backupHint: One password-protected backup file with every account, its cookie and its groups.
settings.aboutHint: MTwin Manager talks to roblox.com, to GitHub to look for its own updates (unless turned off above) and to Discord once you set a webhook, and changes nothing on your PC unless you apply a bandwidth limit. New versions are on GitHub Releases.
settings.setMasterText: MTwin Manager will ask for it at start and after auto-lock.

settings.removeMasterDone: Master password removed. The vault now opens with Windows.
settings.exportText: The file holds every cookie, encrypted with this password. You need it to import the file.
settings.moveDialog: Choose a folder for MTwin Manager's data
settings.selfUpdateHint: Asks GitHub Releases at start and every 6 hours. A new version is offered, never installed without your click, and its installer runs only if it carries MTwin Manager's release signature.
settings.clientInstallHint: Downloads Roblox's installer from setup.rbxcdn.com and runs it once it is verified as signed by Roblox Corporation
settings.backgroundHint: Your own picture behind the app (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, up to 8 MB). It is kept in MTwin Manager's data.

settings.updateConfirmText_other: MTwin Manager closes while it updates and starts again by itself. {count} Roblox clients keep running, and the restarted MTwin Manager follows them again. Their CPU limits are lifted for the few seconds MTwin Manager is closed.

launch.limits.help: The limit is a share of all CPU cores; its frame rate drops with it. For a fixed frame rate, use the FPS cap when launching. Efficiency mode lowers its priority, as Task Manager does. Trimming asks Windows to page its memory out; it comes back as used. Limits set here win over the adaptive manager's. Anti-AFK briefly brings this client to the front for a Space press while you're away; it skips a minimized client.

launch.kill.hint: Hold for a second: ends every Roblox client at once, without saving
launch.multi.turnOnText: Roblox says it doesn't officially support running several clients at once. MTwin Manager only holds the name Roblox's client checks when it starts and never touches the client itself, which Roblox says its enforcement against modified clients doesn't cover. Roblox has broken multi-instance before and may again.
launch.multi.closeText_one: Every running Roblox client closes ({count} process), including ones MTwin Manager didn't start. Unsaved progress in those games is lost.
launch.multi.closeText_other: Every running Roblox client closes ({count} processes), including ones MTwin Manager didn't start. Unsaved progress in those games is lost.
launch.multi.takeOverTitle: Take over from the running Roblox?
launch.multi.takeOverText_one: MTwin Manager closes Roblox's own "already running" marker inside the running client ({count} process) with a standard Windows call, so new clients can start next to it without closing it. Nothing in the client's memory is changed, but this reaches into a running Roblox: if a client misbehaves afterwards, close Roblox instead. Roblox's anti-cheat may see the access.
launch.multi.takeOverText_other: MTwin Manager closes Roblox's own "already running" marker inside the running clients ({count} processes) with a standard Windows call, so new clients can start next to it without closing it. Nothing in the client's memory is changed, but this reaches into a running Roblox: if a client misbehaves afterwards, close Roblox instead. Roblox's anti-cheat may see the access.

discord.intro: Get told in a Discord channel when a client crashes, gets disconnected or is relaunched. MTwin Manager posts to a webhook you create in the channel's settings (Integrations, Webhooks). Discord is the only place besides Roblox MTwin Manager sends anything to, and only once a webhook is set. Messages name accounts by display name and username; never a cookie, link or log.

vault.forgot: Forgot it? It can't be recovered. To start over, close MTwin Manager, delete the database files (the .db file and its .db.key) from the app's data folder in %LOCALAPPDATA%, and add your accounts again.
performance.hintTinyOnLaunch: Each new client goes to the tiny size once it reaches a game. Full quality accounts keep their size.
vault.recovery.showText: It is shown only this once. If you forget your master password, it lets you set a new one. It works once, and then you get a new code.
vault.recovery.copied: Copied. The clipboard clears itself shortly.
vault.recovery.limitFile: A code file on this PC opens your vault for anyone who finds it. Keep it on a USB stick, a phone or paper.
vault.recovery.limitPc: It works only for this Windows user on this PC. After a Windows reinstall or on a new PC it won't help; a backup file does.
vault.recovery.forgotText: Enter your recovery code and choose a new master password. The code then stops working and you get a new one.
vault.recovery.rowHintOn: A code is set. Replacing it stops the old one working.
vault.recovery.rowHintOff: Optional. A code lets you set a new master password if you forget this one.
vault.recovery.offerText: Optional. If you forget the master password, this code lets you set a new one. Without it, the vault can't be opened.
vault.recovery.replaceText: Enter your master password. The old code stops working straight away.
vault.recovery.createText: Enter your master password. The code is shown only once.
vault.recovery.changeReminder: Your recovery code keeps working after this. If someone else may know the old password, replace the code too.

settings.soundHint: Subtle sounds for clicks, switches and notifications.
accounts.toast.befriendCaptcha: Roblox wants a captcha from {names}: open their session and try again
settings.browserDataHint: What the sign-in and session windows remember, so solved captchas stay solved. Reset it if those windows misbehave; Roblox may ask for a captcha again. Your accounts stay signed in.
settings.browserDataBusy: Close the Roblox sign-in and session windows first
accounts.detail.mainHint: Your own account: listed first, skipped by select-all, and confirmed before removing it or showing its cookie. Only one at a time.
accounts.detail.mainCookieText: @{name} is your MAIN account. Anyone with its cookie can sign in as it, so keep it to yourself.
accounts.detail.fpsCapShort: 5 to 360 FPS when its client starts
settings.protectMainHint: Select all (Ctrl+A, the header box, Launch's Select all) skips your MAIN account. You can still tick it by hand.
accounts.befriendText: {count} accounts will friend each other: {pairs} pairs. Friendships are public on Roblox, so anyone can see these accounts are linked.
accounts.exportText: Cookies to export: {count}. They go into a text file in MTwin Manager's folder, one username:cookie per line, and Explorer opens with the file selected.
accounts.exportWarning: Anyone with this file can sign into these accounts. MTwin Manager deletes it after 10 minutes, but antivirus or cloud sync could copy it before then.
accounts.exportPassword: Enter your master password to export these cookies.
accounts.exportSkipped: Skipped, their cookie couldn't be read: {count}
accounts.exportDeletesAt: MTwin Manager deletes the file at {time}.
accounts.removeMainConfirm: {name} is your MAIN account. Remove it from MTwin Manager anyway?
accounts.mainSkipped: Your MAIN account was left out. Pick it by hand to include it.
accounts.befriendRange: Make friends needs 2 to {max} signed-in accounts.
performance.hintMuteOnLaunch: Each client is muted once it reaches a game. Unmute one in the Windows volume mixer.
performance.adaptiveShort: Limits clients that aren't in front.
performance.fairCapShort: Each client's cap shrinks as more run.
performance.trimShort: Pages client memory out on a schedule.
performance.memThrottleShort: Slows a client down past this size.
performance.memRestartShort: Disconnects and relaunches a client past this size.
performance.previewFpsHint: How often each live preview is redrawn.
performance.previewFpsMore: Higher rates use more CPU, more so with many clients.
performance.bench.title: For this PC
performance.bench.intro: Watches the clients already in a game for about 25 seconds, then suggests what to turn on. Nothing new is launched.
performance.bench.needGame: Start a client and let it reach a game first.
performance.bench.measuring: Measuring… keep your clients in their games.
performance.bench.underLimits: CPU was measured under your current limits, so it may read low.
performance.bench.none: Nothing to change: your settings already fit.
performance.bench.stale: Your settings changed since this measurement. Measure again for suggestions that fit them.
performance.bench.capsRefused: Windows refused CPU caps on this PC, so clients are spread across cores instead.
performance.bench.capsUnknown: CPU caps haven't been tried on this PC yet.
performance.bench.gpuRough: The GPU figure is rough: it adds up each client's busiest engine.
performance.bench.restarts: Memory restarts in the last 7 days: {n}
performance.bench.crashes: Crashes after a long run in the last 7 days: {n}
performance.bench.why.fpsCap: A cap of {fps} FPS cuts each client's CPU and GPU use.
performance.bench.why.fpsCapGpu: Your GPU peaked at {gpu}%, so the cap is a step lower: {fps} FPS.
performance.bench.why.lowGraphics: Your PC is busy with this many clients: the lowest graphics save GPU and CPU.
performance.bench.why.lowGraphicsGpu: Your GPU peaked at {gpu}%: the lowest graphics save most of that.
performance.bench.why.lighterRendering: Lighter graphics flags use much less GPU memory.
performance.bench.why.minimizeOnLaunch: With {n} clients, minimized ones save GPU while you play one.
performance.bench.why.tinyOnLaunch: Tiny {width}×{height} windows draw far fewer pixels, and hidden clients stop drawing.
performance.bench.why.muteOnLaunch: Sound from {n} clients at once is only noise.
performance.bench.why.autoSpread: Spreads {n} clients over your {cores} cores so they don't crowd the same ones.
performance.bench.why.fairCap: The CPU would be over the limit: each background client gets at most {cap}%.
performance.bench.why.adaptive: Background clients are held to {cap}% CPU, with efficiency mode.
performance.bench.why.adaptiveEco: Windows refused CPU caps here, so background clients get efficiency mode only.
performance.bench.why.trimEveryMin: Frees each client's unused memory every {min} minutes.
performance.bench.why.memThrottle: Clients peaked at {peak} MB: one past {mb} MB is slowed down before it fills your RAM.
performance.bench.why.memRestart: The clients would need more RAM than you have: one past {mb} MB is restarted. A restart disconnects it.
performance.bench.why.memRestartCrash: Long runs crashed {crashes} times this week: a client past {mb} MB is restarted first. A restart disconnects it.
performance.bench.why.previewFps: Home's previews at {fps} FPS leave more for the clients.
launch.layoutHint: Each client goes into its own spot on MTwin Manager's monitor once it's in a game, in list order. Fit: as big as all fit. Tiny: tiny-size, as many as fit.
settings.multiShort: One client per account, side by side.
settings.launchArgsShort: Extra words after each launch link.
settings.autoRestartShort: Relaunches a client that crashes or hangs.
settings.antiAfkShort: Keeps idle clients from being kicked.
settings.panicShort: Stops every client, from any app.
settings.shutdownShort: Windows' own timer. It closes every app.
settings.publicShort: Off: no launching on Public networks.
settings.aboutShort: What MTwin Manager connects to, and what it changes.
settings.encryptionMoreMaster: Cookies are sealed with AES-256-GCM, using a key made from your master password with Argon2id. Copying or revealing a cookie asks for that password first.
launch.layoutPreviewHint: Shows on your screen, for a few seconds, where each picked account's window will go and in what order
settings.motionHintOn: Liquid motion: pills flow, pages pour in, controls stretch. Kept on this PC.
settings.motionHintReduced: Fades and progress only; nothing travels, bounces or blurs.
settings.motionHintOff: No animation at all: everything changes at once.
flags.title: Custom FFlags
flags.hint: Your own FastFlags, written to Roblox as each client starts.
flags.more: They go over the rendering flags above, so yours win, and Roblox's file goes back as it was once the client has read it. Roblox only applies flags on its allowlist and ignores the rest. Skipped under Bloxstrap and the like, which keep their own. Per account: each account sets its own in its options.
flags.accountHint: This account's own FFlags, used while custom FFlags are set per account.
flags.note: Roblox only applies FFlags on its allowlist and ignores the rest. Not used under Bloxstrap and the like.
flags.empty: No flags yet. Add one, or paste JSON from Bloxstrap with Edit as JSON.
flags.name: Flag name
flags.badJson: That isn't valid JSON. Paste an object of flag names and values.
flags.badValue: {name} needs a text, number or true/false value.
flags.hintAccount: Each account sets its own in its options, under Accounts.
move.manyText: Already playing: {names}. MTwin Manager closes their clients and joins them here with the others, one after another.
move.title: Move {name}?
move.text: {name} is already playing. MTwin Manager closes its client and joins again here. If it's the same game, it goes to the smallest other server.
move.notice: {name} is already playing. Playing moves its client here, after asking.
accounts.add.queueHint: Log In is pressed for you. If Roblox shows a check, solve it in that window. Close a window to skip its account.
browse.none: Add an account to browse Roblox as it.
settings.lockPurchasesShort: No spending Robux or buying Robux and Premium in Browse. Free items still work.
settings.lockPurchasesHint: In Browse, anything that spends Robux is refused before it reaches Roblox, and the Robux, Premium and billing pages don't open. Getting free items still works. MTwin Manager's own private server purchase is refused too. Purchases inside a game happen in the Roblox client, which MTwin Manager can't block.
browse.blocked.create: Create isn't available in MTwin Manager.
browse.blocked.robux: Purchase blocked: Lock purchases is on (Settings, Security).
browse.blocked.money: Buying Robux or Premium is blocked: Lock purchases is on (Settings, Security).
browse.popularNone: Roblox sent no game lists just now. Try again in a while.
browse.playtimeHint: Time in a game from the clients MTwin Manager launched or followed. Play outside MTwin Manager isn't counted.
browse.playtimeNone: No playtime yet. It adds up while clients MTwin Manager launched are in a game.
browse.blocked.signOut: Signing out isn't available in Browse: it would sign this account out of MTwin Manager too.
browse.busy: A launch is already running. Try again when it's done.
game.listCut: Not the whole list: the game has more than MTwin Manager reads, or Roblox stopped answering.
value.title: Limiteds
value.slow: Counting reads the account's whole inventory, a page a second.
value.noRolimons: No Rolimons values yet. Their list is downloaded when you count; after a failed download, MTwin Manager waits 5 minutes before it tries again.
value.projectedHint: Rolimons thinks its RAP is pushed above what it's worth.
value.homeHint: Count all reads each signed-in account's inventory in turn, slowly, and only when you press it.
settings.rolimonsShort: Adds Rolimons' value, demand and trend to your limiteds. Contacts rolimons.com.
settings.rolimonsHint: When you count an account's limiteds, MTwin Manager downloads Rolimons' public item list from api.rolimons.com (at most every 30 minutes) and adds its value, demand, trend and flags. Only that list is fetched: no user ID, username or cookie is sent. Rolimons isn't part of Roblox, and its terms don't allow automated access without its permission. Off by default.
value.notUpdated: Roblox stopped answering partway through the inventory: the last full count is kept.
game.serversHint: An estimate: players now over the server size.
player.counting: Counting their limiteds… A big inventory takes up to a minute.
player.private: Their inventory is private: Roblox doesn't show their limiteds.
player.busy: Another count is running. Press Count when it's done.
progress.webIntro: A live page of every account's progress that updates every 5 seconds, in any browser. Handy on a second screen or your phone.
progress.webShareHint: Open it from a phone or another PC on the same Wi-Fi. Read-only, and only with the secret link below.
progress.webNewKeyDone: New link made; the old one stops working
progress.webFirewall: If Windows asks, allow MTwin Manager on private networks. Anyone with this link on your network can see the page, so make a new link if you shared it by mistake.
progress.webNoNetwork: This PC doesn't seem to be on a network right now.
progress.sub: Live stats from your alts, sent by a script running in your executor.
progress.scriptLead: Put this in your executor's autoexec folder. Every client then reports to MTwin Manager as soon as it joins, and keeps retrying until MTwin Manager is open.
progress.pcNameHint: Groups accounts into machines. Use one name per PC.
progress.scriptHint: Only clients on this PC can reach MTwin Manager's port.
progress.supportedTip: Set up in MTwin Manager: its own script or catalog reads items and values.
progress.customTip: Not set up yet: only the Every game script reads it (leaderstats).
progress.name: Name
progress.emptyBody: Copy the script into your executor's autoexec folder and join a game. Accounts show up here within a few seconds.
progress.removeText: Only their reports go. An account that reports again comes back.
progress.machinesLead: Pick machines to show only their accounts on every tab.
progress.catalogLead: Add values and items by hand: give them a name, a decal picture and a rarity, or a path the script reads them from.
progress.entryIdHint: What the script reports it as, or any name for a value you read with a path.
progress.entryIdTaken: The Catalog already has this ID.
progress.decalHint: The picture shown for it. Empty: the one the script sends.
progress.readFromHint: Optional. Where the script reads the number, from the player: leaderstats.Coins, PlayerGui.Main.Candy.Amount, ReplicatedStorage.Modules.ProfileData.Materials.Owned.Candy, or Player@Gems for an attribute.
progress.readFromHintItem: Optional. Where the script reads how many the account has, like a value's path.
progress.reportedLead: Click one to name it or give it a decal picture.
progress.addGameHint: Paste the game's roblox.com link, or its place or universe ID. Then set up its Catalog before you play it.
progress.addGameBad: That isn't a Roblox game link or ID.
progress.removeGame: Remove this game from the list
progress.noReportsYet: No account has reported from this game yet. Add the values and items to track in the Catalog, then run the script in the game.
progress.scriptTabLead: Luau the reporter downloads and runs in the game to collect what you want. Saved scripts reach running clients within 30 seconds; no need to rejoin.
progress.scriptGameHint: Runs only in this game, after Every game.
progress.scriptEveryHint: Runs in every game first. By default it reads leaderstats.
progress.scriptSaved: Script saved. Clients pick it up within 30 seconds.
progress.scriptNoRuns: No account has reported from this game yet.
progress.docsCardLoader: Once, in your executor's autoexec folder.
progress.docsCardEvery: Runs first in every game: leaderstats and level.
progress.docsCardGame: Each game's own values, items and stats.
progress.docsTipPc: Give each PC its own PC_NAME: the Website and Sheet sync tell them apart by it.
progress.docsNoteDex: Use Dex (or your executor's explorer) to find the real paths in your game, then change the examples to match.
progress.docsTipSuffix: Numbers games show with suffixes, like 1.5K, $74.3Td or 412 No, are read as real numbers, so totals and sorting work.
progress.docsWarnRemote: Only call remotes that only read data. A remote that changes something (buys, sells, spends) would do it every 10 seconds.
progress.docsLead: Progress reports what your scripts read. Set it up in three parts: the loader in your executor, the Every game script and each game's own script (Script tab). Copy any example and change the paths to your game's.
progress.docsLoaderText: Put it in your executor's autoexec folder once. It loads the newest reporter from MTwin Manager on every join, so it never needs changing.
progress.docsEveryText: A game > Script > Every game. Runs in every game first. This is the default:
progress.docsGameText: Add game (or open one) > Script > This game. Mix any of the examples below. Find the real paths with Dex. Save (Ctrl+S): clients pick it up within 30 seconds, and errors show under Last run.
progress.docsItems: Items with name, rarity and picture
progress.docsHValue: A number: coins, candy, a material. A column and a total.
progress.docsHItem: One item. A count of 0 or less is skipped.
progress.docsHItems: A whole table: { [id] = count }, { [id] = { Count = n } } or a list of ids.
progress.docsHItemsFn: The same, with name, rarity, category and picture per item. Return false to skip one.
progress.docsHFind: The object at a path, or the table a ModuleScript returns.
progress.docsHNum: "1,234", a TextLabel or a Value as a number.
progress.docsHP: The local player, a safe require, and the report being built.
progress.docsPathsText: Names with dots between them. Start with leaderstats… (from the player), Player@Attribute, PlayerGui…, Character…, workspace…, game… or any service like ReplicatedStorage…. Past a ModuleScript, the next names are keys of the table it returns.
progress.docsPicturesText: Only what you give: image = a decal id in value or item, or the Catalog's Decal ID, which always wins.
progress.docsOrderText: Each report: Every game, then This game, then the Catalog's Read from paths. A script that errors stops there; the rest still report.
settings.clientPathShort: Automatic launches Roblox's own client. Bootstrappers found on this PC are listed if you want one instead.
settings.clientPathHint: Automatic launches Roblox's own client (the one from roblox.com), even when a bootstrapper opens Roblox links on this PC. To launch through a bootstrapper such as Bloxstrap, Fishstrap or ExploitStrap, pick it from the list, or choose Other and paste the full path of its .exe, e.g. C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Fishstrap\Fishstrap.exe. A bootstrapper manages Roblox's updates and FFlags itself. If Roblox itself isn't installed, Automatic falls back to the bootstrapper it finds.
updates.sub: Roblox's builds on every platform: what's live, what's coming next, and the one before.
updates.futureHint: Deployed but not live yet: Roblox may update to it soon.
updates.pastHint: The build before the current one, used for downgrading.
updates.upToDateNext: Up to date · an update is coming
updates.credit: Data from WhatExpsAre.Online (weao.xyz), refreshed every minute while this page is open.
settings.updatesShort: New versions come from MTwin Manager's GitHub releases.
executor.label: Executor
executor.short: Keeps Roblox on the version your executor supports.
executor.hint: Pick the executor you use (the list and each one's supported Roblox version come from WhatExpsAre.Online). Update Roblox, auto-update and launches then use that Roblox version instead of the newest: when Roblox updates before your executor, Roblox stays on the version it supports; when your executor updates, Roblox follows. Through a bootstrapper, the bootstrapper decides Roblox's version instead.
executor.unlisted: WhatExpsAre.Online doesn't list this executor now; Roblox follows its newest version.
executor.needsInstall: Roblox needs its version: Update Roblox
executor.yoursHint: Chosen in Settings, Launching: Roblox is kept on the version it supports.
accounts.killNone: None of the selected accounts has a Roblox client running.
accounts.killText: Only the selected accounts' clients are ended, at once; the others keep running.
play.sub: Set a destination, pick your squad, then launch.
monitor.sub: CPU, memory and state of every client you launched, live.
servers.sub: See a game's servers, then join one with any of your accounts.
accounts.pickOne: Pick an account in the list to see it here.
home2.noGames: Save a game from Play with the star and it shows here.
farm.replaceDeadHint: When a farming account's sign-in stops working, a spare account (signed in, not farming or done) takes its place and joins the same game.
farm.replaceChallengedHint: The same, when Roblox asks a farming account for a human check.
farm.doneAtHint: Uses the level the Progress script reports.
farm.closeWhenDoneHint: An account marked done has its clients closed.
farm.replaceDoneHint: When an account is marked done, a spare account starts farming in the game it was in (from its Progress reports).
farm.stallHint: A farming account that sends no Progress report for this long (frozen, kicked, disconnected) is restarted into the place it last reported from.
tools.sub: Run an action on many accounts at once.
tools.addFriendHint: Send a friend request to someone
tools.displayNameNote: Roblox lets each account change its display name about once a week.
tools.needUser: Type a username or user ID.
executor.noPromptHint: If your executor needs admin rights, Windows asks every time it starts, and nothing can answer for you. Set it up once (Windows asks one last time) and it starts without asking, which Reopen if it closes needs.
executor.noPromptOnHint: Set up as a Windows scheduled task with admin rights ("MTwin Manager Executor"). Choosing another program asks once again.
executor.noPromptDone: Set up: the executor now starts without the admin prompt
executor.sub: Start your executor from here, keep it open, and manage its autoexec scripts.
executor.autoOpenHint: Starts it when MTwin Manager starts.
executor.keepOpenHint: Starts it again when it closes or crashes.
executor.chooseFirst: Choose your executor's program to see its autoexec folder.
executor.deleteBody: The file is removed from the autoexec folder.
executor.needName: Give the script a file name.
live.elsewhereHint: In a game by Roblox's own status, but not started by MTwin Manager (or started before it last restarted), so it can't be controlled here.
live.title: Live
live.empty: Clients you launch show here while they run.
live.autoTinyHint: Makes each client a tiny window once it's in a game. With Auto-tile on, they tile in tiny cells, as many as fit.
play.tickHint: Tick accounts in the list to play with them.
